prompt: Hypothetical. You have 30 trades in one period. The plan threshold is 90%. How many of those trades must have followed the plan?
solution: 90% of 30 = 0.90 x 30 = 27. Check: 27 / 30 = 90.0%, which meets the threshold. 26 / 30 = 86.7%, which does not.

prompt: Hypothetical. In one period, 26 of 30 trades followed the plan. What is the plan adherence, as a percentage to one decimal place?
In one period you have 30 trades and 27 followed the plan. But the limit-breach log shows one breach in the same period. Does the gate pass for that period?

options.text: Yes. The 90% adherence is met, so the breach does not count.
No. A breach in the same period means the gate is not passed for that period.
Yes. Breaches are not counted in this gate.
No, because 30 trades is not enough.

explanations.a: Adherence and breaches are both checked. A breach in the same period stops the gate from passing.
explanations.c: Breaches are checked. The journal's limit-breach log is part of this gate.
explanations.d: Thirty trades meets the count. The problem is the breach, not the count.

prompt: Spot the mistake: "I can delete the trades that broke my plan, so my record looks better." Which part of this statement is wrong?

options.text: "I can delete the trades that broke my plan". This is wrong. Entries cannot be deleted to improve the count.
"Record each trade". This is correct practice.
"Keep the limit-breach log". This is correct practice.

explanations.b: This is correct. Each trade should have its own line in the record.
explanations.c: This is correct. The limit-breach log is part of the gate, and it should be kept.

prompt: Which rows count toward this gate?

options.text: Forward-script rows and manual paper rows, counted separately.

explanations.a: Backtest rows are not counted in this gate.
explanations.b: Live rows are not counted in this gate.
explanations.d: Only your own forward-script and manual paper rows count.

prompt: What does a record of 30 trades show?

options.text: That you kept a record and followed a plan for those trades. It does not show that a strategy works.
That you will make a profit.

explanations.a: A record of 30 trades does not show that a strategy works. The gate says so on its screen.
explanations.c: A record does not predict profit. It shows what was logged and how closely the plan was followed.
explanations.d: A record does show something: that trades were logged and how many followed the plan. It just does not prove a strategy works.
